Deployment Standard Operating Procedure
CI/CD pipeline, environments, release windows, canary rollout, rollback and incident response

Abstract. This SOP defines how software is built, tested and released to production at Nexora Technologies. It describes
the environments, the automated CI/CD pipeline, approval gates, release windows, the canary deployment strategy, criteria
for automatic rollback, incident severity levels and the on-call rotation. Following this procedure keeps production changes
traceable and reversible.
Keywords: CI/CD, deployment, canary release, rollback, incident severity, on-call, change management
1. Scope and Principles
• Every production change is traceable to an approved pull request and a change record (CHG ticket) in Jira.
• Deployments are automated; engineers do not deploy from laptops or edit production resources manually.
• Every release must be reversible within 15 minutes.
• Infrastructure is defined as code (Terraform) and applications are deployed with Argo CD on Amazon EKS.

3. CI/CD Pipeline
The pipeline runs in GitHub Actions. A change moves through the stages in Figure 1; any failing stage stops the
pipeline and notifies the author. Code must meet the review and coverage rules in the Coding Standards
(NX-ENG-003) before it can be merged.

5. Deployment Strategy
Stateless services use a canary rollout: the new version first receives 5% of traffic for 15 minutes, then 25% for
15 minutes, and finally 100% (Figure 2). The API Gateway uses blue-green deployment. Database migrations
must be backward compatible with the previous application version (expand, migrate, contract) so that a rollback
never requires a schema rollback.
Figure 2. Canary rollout schedule: 5% for 15 minutes, 25% for 15 minutes, then full rollout.
6. Rollback
Automated monitoring compares the canary against the baseline. A rollback is triggered automatically, or by the
release manager, if any of the following occurs:
• HTTP 5xx error rate above 2% for 5 consecutive minutes.
• p95 latency above 2 times the baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
• Failed health checks on more than 20% of new pods, or a crash loop.

7. Incident Severity and On-Call
Table 3. Incident severity levels.
Level
Definition
Acknowledge within
Update frequency
SEV1

15 minutes

SEV2

30 minutes

SEV3

4 hours
Daily
SEV4
Cosmetic issue or low-impact defect
Next business day

The on-call rotation is weekly and handled by senior engineers (G3 and above) and a secondary engineer in G2.
The primary on-call must be reachable within 10 minutes and able to reach a laptop within 30 minutes. On-call
allowances are described in the Benefits Guide (NX-HR-003). SEV1 and SEV2 incidents require a written
post-mortem within 3 working days, following a blameless format.
8. Checklists
8.1 Pre-Deployment
• Change ticket approved and linked to the pull request; release notes prepared.
• All pipeline stages passed on the exact image being released.
• Rollback plan and database migration compatibility confirmed.
• Customer-facing teams notified for changes visible to customers.
• Release is inside the permitted window in Table 2.
8.2 Post-Deployment
• Smoke tests pass and dashboards show error rate and latency within normal range for 30 minutes.
• Feature flags and configuration verified.
• Release notes published and the CHG ticket closed with the final outcome.
